stem: The conservator used an OPAQUE sleeve so light could not pass through to the print. What does OPAQUE mean here?

choices.text: Blocking the passage of light
Letting some light pass diffusely
Letting light pass clearly
Reflecting every sound

explanation: The physical sense of opaque is not transmitting light. Translucent and transparent sleeves permit light; sound reflection is a different property.

stem: A date discrepancy was MATERIAL to deciding which contract applied. Which meaning fits MATERIAL?

choices.text: Made of cloth
Widely circulated
Significant to the issue
Recently discovered

explanation: The adjective concerns importance/consequence for the decision, not physical fabric, circulation or recency.

stem: A guide shook each visitor’s hand but did not look up from his screen; he later spent ten minutes answering a visitor’s questions carefully. A note calls only the greeting PERFUNCTORY. Which interpretation preserves the word and its scope?

choices.text: The greeting was mechanical or superficial; that description need not apply to his later careful answers
The greeting was mechanical or superficial; his later answers therefore lacked care as well
The greeting was warmly attentive; his later answers alone were mechanical
The greeting was delayed; his later answers were therefore brief

explanation: Perfunctory describes routine/superficial performance. The note limits this judgment to the greeting; it does not erase the care explicitly shown later or refer simply to lateness.

stem: The mediator follows the case closely but owns no stake in either outcome. The account calls her DISINTERESTED. Which interpretation fits this use?

choices.text: Impartial despite paying attention
Uninformed because she lacks a stake
Indifferent because she follows the case
Biased because she knows the facts

explanation: The context selects freedom from personal interest or bias. It does not use the word to mean bored; close attention is compatible with impartiality.

stem: Machine X costs less to buy; machine Y costs more but wastes much less fuel. The report calls Y more ECONOMICAL over five years. Which inference preserves the word’s scope?

choices.text: Y uses resources more efficiently over that period, although its purchase price is higher
Y must have the lower initial price because economical means cheap to buy
Y must operate faster because economical means rapid
Y must have the simpler mechanism because economical means uncomplicated

explanation: Economical concerns prudent resource use or savings in operation. The specified five-year perspective allows a higher initial price; speed and mechanical simplicity are not entailed.

stem: The map note calls the boundary EQUIVOCAL because two readings remain possible. It calls the chosen route PROVISIONAL: the route is stated clearly but will be reviewed after a survey. Which revision preserves both distinctions?

choices.text: The boundary permits competing readings; the route is clearly stated but temporary
The boundary permits competing readings; the route is a permanent commitment despite review
The boundary has one settled reading; the route is clearly stated but temporary
The boundary has one settled reading; the route is a permanent commitment despite review

explanation: Equivocal concerns competing interpretations; provisional concerns temporary status. A clear temporary choice need not be ambiguous, and choosing it does not settle the separate boundary.
